2608.19025.title: Self-prompting and cross-model consensus enable reproducible data extraction from scientific literature with large language models
2608.19025.paper_summary: Accurately extracting nuanced, contextualized data from research articles is laborious and time intensive. Here, we investigate the performance of frontier, browser-based large language models (LLMs) to extract highly contextualized information. We demonstrate four escalating workflows, 1) given an expert curated prompt and research articles, most frontier LLMs perform well at data extraction, however can struggle with interpreting scientific context and nuance, 2) given simple instructions, LLMs can author their own prompts which were almost as eNective as expert-written prompts, 3) autonomous discovery of research literature was diNicult, agents either missed or hallucinated references, and 4) LLMs can create new datasets from published guidelines that closely match human-expert judges, but still require a human-in-the-loop. Together, these findings define an auditable division of labour in which experts specify the evidence standard, models cross-check repeated extractions and researchers resolve disputed cases, providing a practical route to scaling scientific data curation without relinquishing expert oversight.
2608.19025.paper_summary_zh: 準確地從研究文章中提取細緻且具上下文的數據是勞動密集且耗時的。在這裡，我們研究了前沿的基於瀏覽器的大型語言模型（LLMs）在提取高度上下文信息方面的表現。我們展示了四個逐步升級的工作流程：1）在專家精心策劃的提示和研究文章的情況下，大多數前沿LLMs在數據提取方面表現良好，但在解釋科學上下文和細微差別時可能會遇到困難，2）在給予簡單指示的情況下，LLMs可以創作自己的提示，這些提示的效果幾乎與專家撰寫的提示相當，3）自主發現研究文獻是困難的，代理人要麼錯過了參考文獻，要麼產生了幻覺，4）LLMs可以從已發表的指導方針中創建新的數據集，這些數據集與人類專家評審的結果非常接近，但仍然需要人類參與。這些發現共同定義了一種可審計的勞動分工，其中專家指定證據標準，模型交叉檢查重複的提取，而研究人員解決有爭議的案例，提供了一條在不放棄專家監督的情況下擴展科學數據策展的實用途徑。
